name: Repeating Characters of a String (Case 2)
description: Construct a program that has a function that receives a string and creates a new string that has every other character of the given string, starting with the first character, repeated two times.\nFor example, the new string that will be formed from the string 'abcde' is 'aaccee'.
code:
#Step 1: Define the function
def double_char(s):
    #Step 1.1: Assign initial value to the variable that we need for the new string
    new_s = ""
    #Step 1.2: Iterate through every other characters in the given string
    for i in range(0, len(s), 2) :
        #Step 1.2.1: Add the repeated character to the the new string
        new_s += s[i] * 2
    #String 1.3: Print the new string
    print(new_s)
#Step 2: Call the function
double_char("Hi There")

comments.content:
We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function double_char that receives a string and creates a new string that has every other character of the given string, starting with the first character, repeated two times. The given string is referred by variable s.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented.
This statement sets variable new_s to the empty string. Later, we will update the content of this variable as we iterate through the characters in the given string.

We want to iterate over every other characters in the given string, starting from the first character, and add each character repeated two times to the new string. We can achieve this by iterating over the index of the characters in the given string and then access the character at each index. We need the indexes to start at 0 (index of the first character) with every second integer number up to but not including the string length. We get this sequence by calling the range(0,len(s),2) function.

The last number in the range function specifies how much to increase each successive integer in the sequence, if this is omitted then step defaults to 1. Since we want to access every other character in the string, we set the step to 2.
Note that len(s) returns the number of the characters in the string. Also note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header.

This statement concatenates the string value stored in variable new_s with the character at the index i of the given string repeated two times. The result of the concatenation is stored in variable new_s.

The repetition operator * repeats the character at index i of the given string for the specified number of times. Also, note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined.

The += operator concatenates the string value stored in variable new_s with the character at the index i of the string repeated two times and the result is stored in the variable new_s. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement new_s = new_s + s[i] * 2.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the new string that is stored in variable new_s. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
This statement calls the double_char function and passes the string "Hi There" as its argument. Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared.
